questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a professional drone pilot
The dangers and the many useful new jobs of drones
Why airports want to ban all drones
The history of military aircraft
questions.why: Rob and Neil discuss the risks of drones but also the ways they are bringing benefits.

questions.q: What do the 2016 UK figures show about drones?
options: There were 70 near misses, more than twice the year before
There were 70 crashes with passenger planes
Near misses fell by half compared with the year before
There were 17 near misses near airports
questions.why: Rob says there were 70 near misses in 2016, 'more than double the year before'.

questions.q: Apart from safety near airports, what other risk does Neil mention?
options: Drones being too noisy in cities
Drones being too expensive for most people
People's privacy being invaded by drone cameras
Drones damaging buildings when they fall
questions.why: Neil mentions the risk to privacy when a drone with a camera flies over someone's property.

questions.q: According to Dr Yoge Patel, what has her company used drones for?
options: Delivering parcels to homes in rural areas
Filming wildlife programmes for television
Rescuing swimmers in trouble at sea
Inspecting planes and entering Fukushima
questions.why: She says their drones are used for aircraft inspections and were put into Fukushima.

questions.q: What are UNICEF and the Malawian government testing drones for?
options: Watching for criminals near the borders
Carrying medical supplies to remote places
Checking for leaks in village water pipes
Training soldiers to fly in bad weather
questions.why: Rob says they are testing drones for carrying medical supplies, which could save lives in remote places.

questions.q: What does a Japanese firm plan to do with a drone?
options: Deliver lunch to office workers
Check that employees arrive on time
Clean the windows of its offices
Play music to make staff stop working late
questions.why: The firm plans to force employees out of the office by playing music at them if they work overtime.

questions.q: After hearing all the examples, what is Neil still a little worried about?
options: How drones are controlled by the law
Whether drones will become too cheap
How long drone batteries last
Whether drones can fly in bad weather
questions.why: Neil says he is 'a little concerned about how they are regulated or controlled'.

questions.q: What does Dr Patel suggest about rules for drones?
options: Drones should be banned until the rules are finished
The same strict rules should apply to every drone
Rules should develop with the technology and suit each use
Rules are not needed because drones are safe
questions.why: She says regulation must be 'harmonised' with technology and be proportionate to different uses.
